'''''Stratiotes aloides''''', commonly known as '''water-soldier'''<ref name=BSBI>[https://plantatlas2020.org/atlas/2cd4p9h.w32 ''Stratiotes aloides''] at the BSBI Plant Atlas</ref><ref>{{PLANTS|id=STAL6|taxon=Stratiotes aloides|accessdate=3 December 2015}}</ref> or '''water pineapple''', is a submerged [[aquatic plant]] native to [[Europe]] and northwestern [[Asia]]. In Britain it was once common in East Anglia and still is in many places, particularly wet ditches and healthy ponds.<ref name=BSBI/> It is the only species in the genus ''[[Stratiotes]]''.

==Description==
''Stratiotes aloides'' has a [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]] of serrated [[leaves]], lanceolate, up to 30 cm long in tufts.  White [[flowers]] up to 45 mm across, with many stamens in the male plants, are produced in the summer.<ref name="Parnell">Parnell, J. and Curtis, T. 2012.'' Webb's An Irish Flora'' Cork University press.{{ISBN|978-185918-4783}}</ref>

==Ecological aspects==
In the summer this plant floats on the water surface with the [[leaves]] just above the surface. In the autumn they become covered with a slimy secretion (calcium carbonate) and the whole plant sinks to the bottom to rise again in the spring.<ref> Michael Bright, 1000 Wonders of Nature,(2001) p.339.</ref> Fossils have been found of this plant.{{Citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Plants are dioecious. Male and female plants must be grown if seed is required. Only the female plant occurs naturally in Britain, though plants with hermaphrodite flowers are also found occasionally. Seed is never set in Britain, the plants increasing mainly by offsets.<ref>Clapham, Tutin and Warburg</ref>

==Distribution==
In [[Ireland]], it is found in shallow waters where it was introduced.<ref name="Parnell"/> Apparently now extinct in the north-east of Ireland.<ref>Hackney, P. (ed) 1992. ''Stewart & Corry's Flora of the North-east of Ireland.'' Institute of Irish Studies, The Queen's University of Belfast. {{ISBN|0-85389-446-9}}</ref> Rare in east England.<ref>Martin, W.K. 1965. ''The Concise British Flora in Colour.'' George Rainbird Ltd.</ref>

===Invasive species===
''Stratiotes aloides'' has been found in the [[Trent River (Ontario)|Trent River]] in eastern [[Ontario]], [[Canada]].<ref>http://www.bqrap.ca/cms_lib/watersoldierPosterLOWRES.PDF {{dead link|date=March 2014}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
Most suitable for the cool [[aquarium]] or [[pond]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2021}}

Propagation from runners which form from the centre of the [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]] of [[leaves]].{{Citation needed|date=May 2021}}

The herb has had a high reputation for treating wounds, especially when these are made by an iron implement. It is applied externally. The plant is also said to be of use in the treatment of [[ergotism]] and also of bruised kidneys.<ref>Grieve, ''A Modern Herbal''. Penguin (1984)</ref>
